title: performance-canary-kv-hysteresis-autodetect-rollout-guards
author: Samira Patel
release_notes: Improves performance canary sensitivity by integrating KV-cache hysteresis into automated detection; reduces false positives during short-lived backend GC events and enables safer canary rollouts.
description:
Context: our continuous performance canary has flagged multiple transient latency regressions over the last quarter that corresponded to short-lived KV-cache GC and eviction spikes. These caused noisy rollouts and unnecessary rollbacks. This PR implements a KV-cache-aware hysteresis layer in the canary detector and adjusts automated rollout guards to reduce false positives while preserving detection of real regressions. Changes include: hysteresis windows per-model/route, dynamic threshold smoothing, and a new config flag to require sustained degradation across both latency and throughput for automated traffic shifts.

Motivation: reduce noise in automatic rollouts, decrease unnecessary fallbacks, and make the detector more robust to transient backend behaviour (GC, short cache churn, and rare cold-starts). This directly improves SLO stability and reduces operational toil.

What I changed: 1) runtime/canary/detector.py: added KVCacheHysteresis class and integrated it into the detector pipeline. 2) runtime/canary/config.yaml: new defaults for hysteresis_window_ms and smoothing_alpha. 3) observability/canary_metrics.go: added metrics for hysteresis state and smoothed latency. 4) perf/canary/test_hysteresis.py and perf/canary/sim_tests: added unit and simulation tests that model GC spikes and cold-starts. 5) console/rollouts: updated rollout guard UI to expose hysteresis tuning and explain trade-offs. 6) docs/perf/canary.md: documented config semantics and suggested tuning recipes.

Behavior and rollout plan: the new detector uses a two-stage rule: (A) immediate alerting for large, sustained regressions; (B) for medium-sized regressions, require hysteresis-confirmation (degradation persists beyond hysteresis_window_ms) and concordance between latency and throughput signals before automated traffic shift. Default hysteresis_window_ms=120000 (2 minutes) with smoothing_alpha=0.2. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout to 10% of controlled namespaces, monitor canary metrics for 72 hours, then progressively enable automated traffic shifts if stable.

Testing: unit tests for hysteresis state transitions, simulation tests that run synthetic GC/cold-start traces through detector, end-to-end smoke in perf-canary lab, and manual verification of console UI flows. CI recorded one flaky integration test initially; rerun passed.

Backwards compatibility: defaults are conservative and the feature is gated behind a config flag (canary.kv_hysteresis.enabled=false by default for existing tenants). No breaking API changes.

Related: Linear ENG-2048 (canary noise reduction), ENG-2101 (console rollout UI), SUP-345 (customer incident that motivated this).

Checklist:
- [x] Add detector logic and unit tests
- [x] Add simulation tests for transient GC spikes
- [x] Expose tuning in Console UI
- [x] Add docs and release notes
- [x] Coordinate staged rollout with SRE

Notes: tuning values were chosen after running 5000+ synthetic traces; customer-facing default remains off until we validate in 10% rollout.
